subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the tangent and the normal to the curve y = 5x⁴ at the point (1, 5).

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what dy/dx is, what the slope is at x = 1, and what you do to that slope to get the normal.

steps.label: Differentiate y = 5x⁴
steps.margin_note: First mark. The constant 5 stays in front; only x⁴ is differentiated. The check y = 5 at x = 1 confirms the point is on the curve.
lines: Check the point: at x = 1,  y = 5(1)⁴ = 5, so (1, 5) lies on the curve.

steps.why: The tangent and the normal both come from this one derivative, so it is written before either line is attempted. A constant multiplier is carried through the power rule unchanged.
common_mistakes: Differentiating 5x⁴ to 5x³, dropping the factor 4 that the power rule produces.
Writing 20x⁴, reducing the coefficient but not the index.
Differentiating the number 5 as well and adding a stray term.
steps.memory_tip: Power rule on 5x⁴: multiply the 5 by the power 4 to get 20, then lower the power to 3.

steps.label: Slope at (1, 5) and the tangent
steps.margin_note: Two marks: one for m = 20 with its substitution line, one for the tangent written in general form. Quote y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) before putting numbers in.
lines: The slope of the tangent is dy/dx at the given point.
Tangent at (x₁, y₁) with slope m:   y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

recall.must_convey: That m = 20 at x = 1, and the tangent is 20x − y − 15 = 0.

steps.why: dy/dx gives a different slope at each point, so it has to be evaluated at x = 1 before it can be used. The point-slope form then needs nothing beyond the point and that number.
common_mistakes: Substituting y = 5 into 20x³ instead of x = 1.
Writing 20x − y + 15 = 0, losing the sign when moving −5 across.
steps.memory_tip: At x = 1 every power of x is 1, so the slope is just the coefficient. Here that coefficient is 20.

steps.label: Equation of the normal
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The normal's slope is −1/m = −1/20, not −20. Multiply by 20 to clear the fraction, then check: 1 + 100 − 101 = 0 at (1, 5).
lines: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent at the same point,

recall.must_convey: That the normal's slope is −1/20, giving x + 20y − 101 = 0.

the normal and the tangent are perpendicular at one comma five

steps.why: A steep tangent gives a shallow normal: slope 20 becomes −1/20. The reciprocal alone is not enough — the sign has to change as well.
common_mistakes: Using −20 as the normal's slope instead of −1/20.
Writing +1/20, doing the reciprocal but not the sign change.
Arithmetic slip on −100 + 1, giving −99 instead of the correct constant.
steps.memory_tip: Turn 20 into 1/20 and change the sign. A steep tangent always has a flat normal.

insider_note: m = 20x³ gives 20 at x = 1 — a steep tangent and a very flat normal of slope −1/20. Both equations are asked for, so write both.
